newsitem.title: USA: Court lowers Occidental unit's damages.
newsitem.headline: Court lowers Occidental unit's damages.

text.p: A federal appeals court on Tuesday lowered a jury's punitive damage award against Oxy USA Inc, a unit of Occidental Petroleum Corp, by $24 million to $6 million.
The appeals court last year had upheld the original judgement, but reversed itself in light of a recent U.S. Supreme Court decision, the appeals court said.

Earlier this year, the Supreme Court held that a $2 million punitive damage award against Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG (BMW) for failing to disclose to a buyer that his new car had been repainted was too large.

Oxy was sued for interference with contracts related to gathering of natural gas from plantiffs' wells in Oklahoma in 1992. The appeals court said the original $30 million judgement was "grossly excessive" under standards of the Supreme Court decision.
Suing Oxy were Continental Trend Resources Inc, Ferrar Oil Co, and three individuals and a trust.

The jury had awarded the plantiffs $269,000 for actual damages and the $30 million in punitive damages and found that Oxy had "intentionally interfered with the plantiffs' existing and prospective contracts", the appeals court said.
